method.method_draft: Use the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus directly. From the image, first read the values of the plotted function at the interval endpoints: the graph is horizontal at y=2 from x=2 to x=4, so f(3)=2; the graph ends on the x-axis at x=8, so f(8)=0. From the text, the requested quantity is \(\int_3^8 f'(x)\,dx\). Apply \(\int_a^b f'(x)\,dx=f(b)-f(a)\), giving \(f(8)-f(3)=0-2=-2\).

method.method_draft: Compute the integral by treating f'(x) as the slope of each linear piece. From the image, on x=3 to x=4 the graph is horizontal at y=2, so f'(x)=0 and the contribution is 0. From x=4 to x=6 the graph drops from 2 to -2, so the slope is \((-2-2)/(6-4)=-2\), giving contribution \(-2\cdot 2=-4\). From x=6 to x=8 the graph rises from -2 to 0, so the slope is \((0-(-2))/(8-6)=1\), giving contribution \(1\cdot 2=2\). Add the contributions: \(0-4+2=-2\).
